top_choice_rationale: Mircea Cărtărescu alone (P001) is the best-supported literary case on the slate. From public knowledge of Blinding (the Orbitor sequence) and Solenoid, his voice is distinctive and his formal achievement lies in very large, nested structures with recurring image systems, in which memory, the body and dream form one metaphysical project. The imaginative depth is considerable, and the oeuvre looks consolidated, so premature judgment is not the concern. The citation should rest on the prose, with poetry named only as a root, because translated coverage of the poetry and early work is thin. My own test, whether the late novels deepen their image systems or only recirculate them, remains unsettled from translation and public knowledge. I treat that as the main risk, a limit of access and not a finding against the work. The six-member convergence is not evidence of merit. P000 ranks second because the reservations concern evidence and translation, not the writer's significance, and they apply to every candidate. This judgment rests on general public knowledge and colleagues' stated views, not on independently verified reading.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; documented connections are to Selma Lagerlöf as a biographical subject, collaborator Kate Larson, David Håkansson (elected with her in 2023) and committee colleagues, none involving Cărtărescu. Her own practice is context, not evidence of preference.
